newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and bellies close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and bellies close mostly lower.

text.p: CME lean hog futures closed mostly lower despite strength in the cash market while bellies also finished mostly down.
Floor sources noted that August was weakened late by selling linked to the "Goldman roll," Goldman Sachs commodity index fund's practice of rolling its long nearby positions into the next month.
Hot, humid weather in the U.S. Midwest curbed hog marketings on Monday and prices at interior markets were $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher. Prices were expected to be steady to $0.50 higher on Tuesday.

"Cash was up and will be up a little more tomorrow (Tuesday) but I guess hot weather is only going to last so long," one dealer said, noting cash prices could quickly slip back down if weather conditions improve.
Pork belly futures were mostly lower as the market gave up some of the ground gained late last week.
"We just ran out of buyers," a floor source said, noting there continued to be expectations that cash fresh belly prices should strengthen this week.
An already-light hog slaughter should be slowed further by the reduction in hog marketings linked to the hot spell.
August bellies closed 0.500 cent a lb lower at 80.250 cents with other months up 0.225 cent to off 1.800 cent.
In hog options Rand Financials was a featured seller of December puts with a strike price of 68 cents, traders said.
